articles.title: Aave Labs Buys Avon Team to Build Fixed-Rate Lending
articles.excerpt: Terms were not disclosed. Fixed-rate markets are planned work, not a live Aave product in Friday's post, which cites over $33B in deposits.
articles.body_md:
Aave Labs said Friday it has acquired the team and technology behind Avon, a startup that built fixed-rate and floating-rate lending markets and an onchain order book, as the network works to add fixed-rate loans to a platform it says holds more than $33 billion in deposits.

The [Aave Labs blog post](https://aave.com/blog/avon-acquisition) does not disclose financial terms. Prince Sinha and Ayush Kaul are joining the Labs engineering team, and Omar el-Ashaal is joining business development. Avon's fixed- and floating-rate protocols, order book, domains and related assets move with the team. [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/blockchain/2026/aave-labs-acquires-avon-tech-to-take-on-chain-lending-mainstream/) reported the same deal from a Friday release.

**How fixed-rate lending differs onchain**

Most large DeFi lending pools, including Aave's core markets, set borrow rates that float with supply and demand. A fixed-rate loan locks the interest cost for a set term, the way many bank mortgages and corporate credit lines work. Avon's order book was built to match lenders and borrowers for those structures while isolating risk by strategy. Fixed-rate markets on Aave are planned work. Friday's post does not describe a live fixed-rate product.

Aave Labs describes Aave as the largest onchain lending network, with more than $33 billion in deposits and more than $13 billion in active loans in the blog post (an about section on the same page cites more than $30 billion in net deposits). The network is governed by the Aave DAO; Friday's buyer is the Labs contributor entity. The post does not describe a DAO treasury purchase.

"Aave's goal is to bring the best of finance to everyone, and that means offering the kinds of products users already rely on, including fixed rates," founder and CEO Stani Kulechov said in the post. Sinha said the team wants to keep building credit-market depth where it can reach institutions, fintechs and everyday users at scale.

*In our opinion: Aave is buying the team that was already wiring bank-style fixed rates into DeFi, and the price tag stays off the page. That is one way to skip a multi-year build. What to watch next is a public timeline, a test deployment of the order book, or an Aave DAO vote on parameters once Labs is ready to ship.*

articles.title: GOPAX Halts Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
articles.excerpt: Withdrawals stopped at 2:55 p.m. local time and trading at 3:53 p.m. Assets are moving to cold wallets; no loss has been reported.
articles.body_md:
South Korean crypto exchange GOPAX suspended withdrawals at 2:55 p.m. local time Friday and halted trading at about 3:53 p.m. after receiving an email that claimed the platform had been hacked, the exchange said.

No asset loss has been reported. GOPAX said it had not verified whether the threat was genuine and was moving assets from hot wallets into offline cold storage as a precaution, [Yonhap News Agency](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261106011751320) reported. The [Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10928990) carried the same account.

**What a hot-to-cold shift does**

A hot wallet stays online so the exchange can process customer sends quickly. A cold wallet is kept offline, cut off from the internet, which shrinks the surface an attacker can reach if they have access to online systems. GOPAX said it is transferring remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage first, then checking security. Standard withdrawals through the website and app are off. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are handled manually after internal checks. All open orders were canceled when trading stopped. Deposits of virtual assets were also paused. The company has not set a date to reopen services.

A GOPAX official told Yonhap the email came from a group claiming to have hacked the exchange. "We are prioritizing the protection of customers' assets, even if this causes inconvenience to users," the official said.

The move lands as South Korea's financial sector digests a wider cybersecurity wave. The Financial Services Commission earlier confirmed incidents at 37 financial institutions that affected about 470,000 customer records, Yonhap said. Separately, Korean coverage has noted earlier personal-information leaks at GOPAX this fall; a link between those leaks and Friday's email has not been confirmed.

*In our opinion: customers face stalled access while GOPAX verifies the email and finishes the cold-wallet move. No loss is reported. The next checkable item is the date the exchange restores standard withdrawals and trading; until then, manual support-desk requests are the only path out.*

articles.title: FinCEN Cuts MEXC Off U.S. Finance Over $16B Illicit Claim
articles.excerpt: The order under section 9714 takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication. MEXC had not issued a public response by late Friday ET.
articles.body_md:
FinCEN on Friday ordered U.S. financial institutions to stop processing funds transfers to or from MEXC Global, saying the offshore crypto exchange facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions from May 2021 through May 2026.

The [Treasury press release](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0685) frames the cut-off as part of Operation Economic Outcast. The order rests on section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. It takes effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. It is a funds-transmittal ban under FinCEN rules. It is separate from an OFAC sanctions listing and does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act or OFAC duties.

**How a 9714 cut-off works**

Section 9714 lets FinCEN bar covered U.S. banks and money transmitters from moving dollars or convertible virtual currency to or from a named foreign exchanger found to be of primary money laundering concern tied to Russian illicit finance. Once the clock starts, those firms face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. MEXC already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its terms, so the practical hit is remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still clear through U.S. institutions.

Treasury says MEXC processed more than $1 billion a day and held about $5 billion in reserves as of September 2026, ranking among the world's 20 largest crypto exchangers. The release alleges nearly $1.5 billion in flows linked to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million in direct trades with U.S.-, EU- and UK-sanctioned entities, and continued activity with OFAC-designated Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026. It also cites about $1 billion in direct traffic with more than 40 Iranian crypto exchangers and roughly $22 million tied to Iran's Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Qods Force.

MEXC had not issued a public response to the Friday order by late afternoon ET, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/fincen-cuts-off-mexc-us-financial-system) reported, noting the exchange's main X account kept posting marketing content through the afternoon. The Federal Register index had not yet posted the notice as of Friday evening, so the 30-day fuse had not started.

*In our opinion: the Register clock is the number that starts the ban. Until that notice posts, covered banks still have a countdown ahead. Watch whether MEXC contests the finding, seeks an exemption, or reroutes liquidity away from U.S. rails once the order bites.*

articles.title: Ex-FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to $2.47 Million Crypto Theft
articles.excerpt: Prosecutors say about 100 transfers used credentials tied to 35 FBI cases. Sentencing is set for March 4, 2027, with a maximum of 20 years.
articles.body_md:
Former FBI agent Patrick Steven Yaroch pleaded guilty on Nov. 5 to wire fraud and money laundering over the theft of about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Virginia said, according to [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/ex-fbi-agents-plea-puts-crypto-theft-at-2-47-million-over-twice-what-he-first-told-the-fbi/) and [FOX 5 DC](https://www.fox5dc.com/news/ex-fbi-agent-pleads-guilty-2-5m-cryptocurrency-theft-scheme-where-he-chatgpt-how-flee-portugal).

Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Va., entered a plea covering roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using wallet credentials linked to 35 FBI investigations, prosecutors said in the plea materials summarized by those outlets. The wallets included accounts tied to subjects of other probes, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI built for an operation, the agreed statement of facts says, as reported.

**How prosecutors describe the scheme**

Yaroch had access to FBI systems that stored crypto credentials collected in investigations. Beginning no later than December 2024, he moved funds out of those wallets, converted them into other tokens and ran further transactions to disguise the trail, according to the plea's statement of facts. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts and used funds to pay debts such as card balances and car payments, Unchained reported from the Justice Department materials.

The $2.47 million figure is more than double what he first told FBI headquarters in July, when an affidavit recounted his claim of about 10 transfers into a wallet holding roughly $1 million. The [Justice Department Office of the Inspector General](https://oig.justice.gov/news/press-release/fbi-supervisory-special-agent-arrested-following-theft-cryptocurrency) said he was arrested Aug. 4 on a criminal complaint in the Eastern District of Virginia after self-reporting activity in late July. Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea (Case No. 1:26-CR-208). Sentencing is set for March 4, 2027. He faces up to 20 years in prison.

Sentencing is March 4, 2027. The plea locks in the $2.47 million figure and the 35-case credential count that the July self-report understated.

articles.title: DOL Crypto 401(k) Rule Enters Final White House Review
articles.excerpt: RIN 1210-AC38 is a final-rule package from Labor's EBSA, separate from the SEC crypto broker draft reviewed this week. The final text is not public yet.
articles.body_md:
A U.S. Department of Labor final rule on how 401(k) fiduciaries pick investment options, including vehicles that can hold crypto, entered White House review on Nov. 5, an [Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs listing](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/eoDetails?rrid=1591871) shows.

The package is titled "Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives" (RIN 1210-AC38). It is staged as a final rule from Labor's Employee Benefits Security Administration, flagged economically significant, and carries no legal deadline. This is a different file from the SEC crypto broker-dealer draft (RIN 3235-AN48) that entered review earlier this week.

**What the March proposal offered**

Labor published the proposal on March 30. Under that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding alternative assets to a 401(k) menu would receive a process-based safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named were performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, benchmarks and complexity, [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/dol-rule-crypto-401k-white-house-review) reported, summarizing the DOL proposal and a department fact sheet.

A safe harbor does not require plans to offer crypto. It lowers litigation risk for committees that choose exposure through an allocation sleeve that can hold digital assets, private equity or real estate. The March draft followed President Trump's Aug. 7, 2025, executive order directing Labor to reexamine ERISA guidance on alternative assets in defined-contribution plans. In May 2025 the department had already rescinded a 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use "extreme care" before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu.

OIRA review under Executive Order 12866 is the last interagency stop before a final rule can be published in the Federal Register. The final wording, any changes to the six-factor test and the effective date will be clear only when Labor posts the cleared text.

*In our opinion: agency and RIN are the map here. Labor's ERISA fiduciary file (1210-AC38) sits apart from the SEC broker rewrite (3235-AN48). The next document to watch is the Federal Register final rule once OIRA returns the Labor package.*

articles.title: Strive Posts $509 Million Q3 Profit on Bitcoin Fair-Value Gains
articles.excerpt: Net unrealized gains on digital assets were $533.7 million in the quarter. The firm bought another 15,124 bitcoin from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30.
articles.body_md:
Strive, Inc. reported GAAP net income of $509.0 million for the three months ended Sept. 30, or $5.24 per diluted common share, driven mainly by bitcoin marked to fair value, the company said in a [GlobeNewswire release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/06/3397482/0/en/strive-inc-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results.html) Friday.

Net unrealized gains on digital assets at fair value were $533.7 million in the quarter. Total revenues were only $2.7 million, mostly investment advisory fees and medical-device sales, so the profit line reflects fair-value marks on the bitcoin book. Operating cash from fees was a thin slice beside it.

**How the bitcoin book moved**

Strive is a Nasdaq-listed firm (ticker ASST) that runs a bitcoin treasury alongside an asset-management unit. Under U.S. crypto accounting rules (ASU 2023-08), bitcoin on the balance sheet is carried at fair value, with gains and losses flowing through net income each period. That means a rising bitcoin price can print a large quarterly profit even when operating revenue is small, and the reverse when prices fall.

The company said it acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter and 20,373 bitcoin in the nine months through Sept. 30. It bought another 15,124 bitcoin from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30. Digital assets stood at about $2.34 billion fair value on Sept. 30. On Oct. 20 it completed a registered offering of 7 million shares of its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS preferred stock for about $609 million in net proceeds.

Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole said in the release that Strive's year-to-date bitcoin yield is, in his view, the main driver of common equity outperformance versus bitcoin this year. Non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to common stockholders was $494.6 million, or $5.46 per diluted share, after preferred dividends and other adjustments the company defines.

Bitcoin was about $75,920 around noon ET Friday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the $533.7 million fair-value gain did the heavy lifting beside $2.7 million of revenue. A $509 million profit on a fee book that size is the fair-value rule doing what it says on the tin. Readers watching treasury peers can next check how many bitcoin Strive discloses after October's 15,124-coin add when the next balance sheet lands.*

articles.title: Gnosis Pay Says Hackers Accessed Branded-Card Customer Data
articles.excerpt: The company did not say how many customers were hit. It made 3D Secure mandatory for online card payments until the consumer system retires Dec. 20.
articles.body_md:
Gnosis Pay said Friday that unauthorized access on Nov. 3 exposed certain customer information on the legacy system behind its own branded cards, according to a [company blog post](https://gnosispay.com/blog/data-breach-legacy-system-gnosis-pay-branded-cards).

Containment began within two hours of detection, the firm said. It replaced affected security credentials and fixed the vulnerability. Customer funds were not affected, Gnosis Pay wrote. Its enterprise platform that powers white-label card programs for partners was not hit.

**What changed for card users**

Gnosis Pay is a crypto card provider: users spend stablecoin or crypto balances through a Visa-linked debit card. The breached stack was the B2C branded-card system, already set to retire on Dec. 20, 2026. Until then, the company made 3D Secure, an extra step that confirms online card payments, mandatory for all online charges. It also said it stepped up monitoring of card activity and wallets for fraud.

The firm emailed every affected customer with the specific data taken from their account, reported the incident to partners, the card issuer and data-protection authorities, and said it is arranging specialist monitoring for misuse. It did not publish a headcount of affected customers or a full inventory of data types in the public post.

[Protos](https://protos.com/gnosis-pay-breach-exposes-customer-addresses/) reported that some customer emails described exposure that can include names, shipping or home addresses, card details and linked wallet addresses, citing screenshots shared by users. Gnosis Pay advised customers to treat unexpected messages about their cards as suspect, never share seed phrases, PINs or full card numbers, and be careful sharing home addresses or crypto holdings online or offline.

Gnosis Pay said every affected customer received an email listing exactly what was taken from their account. The consumer branded-card system is still scheduled to retire on Dec. 20.

articles.title: U.S. Adds 165,000 Jobs in October as Unemployment Hits 4.1%
articles.excerpt: August and September payrolls were revised up by a combined 84,000. CME FedWatch odds of a December quarter-point hike rose to about 76.8%.
articles.body_md:
U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October and the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, the [Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm) reported at 8:30 a.m. ET Friday.

The payroll gain beat the Dow Jones consensus for about 59,000 new jobs cited by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/jobs-report-october-2026.html). BLS said professional and business services led with 70,000 jobs, health care added 42,000, transportation and warehousing 25,000 and manufacturing 19,000. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month to $38.00, up 3.1% over 12 months.

**How the report feeds the Fed**

The Employment Situation mixes two surveys. The establishment survey counts payroll jobs by industry. The household survey drives the unemployment rate. Stronger hiring and a firmer wage print can keep inflation pressure in view, which is why rate futures often reprice after the release.

August payrolls were revised up by 53,000 to 186,000 and September by 31,000 to 60,000, BLS said, a combined 84,000 more jobs than previously reported. The labor force participation rate stood at 61.9%. People working part time for economic reasons rose by 339,000 to 4.8 million.

After the print, CME Group's FedWatch tool showed about a 76.8% chance of a quarter-point rate increase at the Dec. 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, CNBC reported, up from levels before the release. A [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/traders-raise-bets-of-fed-rate-hike-after-jobs-report-5008229) dispatch put futures pricing near an 80% probability of a December hike.

Bitcoin was about $75,920 around noon ET Friday (down about 0.6% over 24 hours), per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: for crypto readers, the stake sits at the December FOMC. A higher overnight rate can tighten liquidity for non-yielding assets. The next hard check is the Fed's own statement on Dec. 9.*

articles.title: FinCEN and Fed Withdraw $250 Cross-Border Travel Rule Plan
articles.excerpt: The 2020 proposal also sought to spell out Travel Rule coverage for convertible virtual currency. Publication of the withdrawal is set for Nov. 9.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Federal Reserve Board are withdrawing a 2020 plan that would have cut the threshold for collecting, retaining and transmitting information on cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250, a [Federal Register public-inspection notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-22809/threshold-for-the-requirement-to-collect-retain-and-transmit-information-on-funds-transfers-and) filed Friday shows.

The agencies said they will not take further action on the joint notice of proposed rulemaking published Oct. 27, 2020. The withdrawal is scheduled for Federal Register publication on Nov. 9. The existing $3,000 Recordkeeping Rule and Travel Rule thresholds stay in place.

**What the 2020 plan would have changed**

Under Bank Secrecy Act rules often called the Recordkeeping Rule and the Travel Rule, banks and nonbank financial institutions must collect, keep and pass on sender and recipient details for funds transfers of $3,000 or more. The 2020 proposal would have lowered that bar to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. FinCEN also proposed clarifying that "money" in those rules covers domestic and cross-border transactions in convertible virtual currency and digital assets with legal tender status.

The agencies received nearly 3,000 comments. Most opposed the lower threshold, citing burden on smaller institutions, remittance costs and weak supporting data, the withdrawal notice says. Views on applying the rules expressly to crypto were mixed: crypto service firms often objected on technology and messaging standards, while some banks and money services businesses supported that piece.

FinCEN and the Fed gave two reasons for pulling the file. More than five years have passed, and they want fresh public comment before any similar rewrite. They also pointed to newer crypto frameworks, including the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted in July 2025, and said future Travel Rule changes for crypto should fit those developments.

*In our opinion: $3,000 is still the live Travel Rule line for these transfers. Nov. 9 is when the withdrawal hits the Federal Register; any crypto-specific rewrite would need a fresh comment round after GENIUS-era stablecoin rules.*

articles.title: Bank of Russia Clears Bitcoin, Ether and USDT for Nov. 17
articles.excerpt: Non-qualified buyers face a 300,000-ruble yearly cap per intermediary. All investors must pass a test and review crypto risks before trading.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Russia on Friday named bitcoin, ether and Tether's USDT as the cryptocurrencies non-qualified investors may buy once a regulator directive takes effect on Nov. 17, the [central bank](https://www.cbr.ru/press/event/?id=32964) said.

From that date, exchanges can list those three assets for public trading. Non-qualified investors can buy them through a broker, asset manager or crypto exchange service, on exchange or over the counter, with a purchase limit of 300,000 rubles (about $3,660) per calendar year through each intermediary, [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/russia-approves-bitcoin-ether-usdt-for-exchange-trading/4114385) reported, matching the Bank of Russia notice.

**How the retail door works**

Russia's crypto framework already bars domestic crypto payments. The new list is the liquidity screen for retail buyers: the central bank said it picked assets by market capitalization, average daily trading volume and at least five years of price history on foreign platforms. Qualified investors face no purchase cap and may buy any crypto asset. Every investor, qualified or not, must pass a test and review crypto investment risks before a trade.

The directive is permissive, not mandatory. Exchanges get the right to list bitcoin, ether and USDT. They are not required to list them. Domestic payments in crypto remain off-limits under the wider law whose main provisions took effect Sept. 1.

Bitcoin was about $75,920 around noon ET Friday, down roughly 0.6% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether was about $2,234, down roughly 1.4% on the same window.

The directive takes effect Nov. 17. The 300,000-ruble yearly cap per intermediary stays the retail limit once listings open.

articles.title: Ukraine Central Bank Won't Back Crypto Bill as Drafted
articles.excerpt: The NBU wants authority to restrict foreign tokens that act like e-money. A final Rada vote is expected later in November.
articles.body_md:
The National Bank of Ukraine said it cannot support Draft Law No. 10225-d on virtual-asset circulation in its current form, citing foreign tokens that can act like electronic money, unequal rules versus domestic assets, and monopolization risks in platform licensing, in a [Nov. 4 statement](https://bank.gov.ua/en/news/all/pozitsiya-natsionalnogo-banku-ukrayini-schodo-zakonoproyektu--10225-d-pro-obig-virtualnih-aktiviv).

A Verkhovna Rada committee recommended the bill for second reading the same day. Lawmakers still have to vote. [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/ukraine-central-bank-refuses-crypto-bill) reported that a final floor vote is expected later in November, with rules taking effect July 1, 2027 if adopted (citing Interfax Ukraine).

**Three risks the NBU listed**

First, the bank said the draft lets foreign tokens into Ukraine even when they perform electronic-money functions without matching supervision where they are issued. It wants authority to assess those tokens and, when needed, restrict their circulation, as it can for domestically issued tokens.

Second, simplified admission of foreign virtual assets must not let them skip requirements that apply to comparable Ukrainian assets, the NBU said, warning of regulatory arbitrage.

Third, it said the final text leaves the number of trading-platform operators in the first five years to the National Securities and Stock Market Commission's discretion without a clear cap or enough antitrust safeguards. The bank had earlier agreed, as a compromise, to a competitive limit of three operators.

**How the bill would split oversight**

Virtual-asset laws set who may issue, trade and custody tokens, and which regulator watches them. Under the committee version described by Bitcoin Magazine, the split would look like this: the securities commission as main market regulator, the NBU over electronic-money tokens. The NBU said it supports MiCA-style rules and IMF recommendations in principle, but that the final draft it received late the evening before the committee vote did not reflect key drafting compromises.

Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban raised the objections at the committee meeting, the NBU said. The bank called on lawmakers to refine the document with all participants.

The next date on the calendar is the floor vote later in November. If the committee text passes, Bitcoin Magazine reported (citing Interfax Ukraine), the rules take effect July 1, 2027.

articles.title: Nigeria Sets N15 Billion Capital Bar for Dollar Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: Naira-referenced issuers need ₦10 billion. Existing operators must register within 30 days of commencement and seek a licence within 180 days.
articles.body_md:
Nigeria's central bank published regulations for non-security virtual assets that require stablecoin issuers to hold a CBN licence, with Class 2 foreign-currency issuers needing minimum paid-up capital of ₦15 billion and Class 1 naira issuers needing ₦10 billion, the [CBN document](https://www.cbn.gov.ng/Out/2026/CCD/REGULATIONS%20FOR%20THE%20OPERATIONS%20OF%20NON-SECURITY%20VIRTUAL%20ASSETS%20IN%20NIGERIA.pdf) dated for the new framework shows.

[Nairametrics](https://nairametrics.com/2026/11/06/cbn-sets-n15-billion-capital-requirement-for-foreign-stablecoin-issuers-tightens-p2p-crypto-rules/) said the rules were issued Nov. 5, 2026. Other non-security virtual-asset service providers face a ₦1 billion capital floor, the PDF's Section 16 states.

**What licensed issuers must do**

Section 15 of the regulations says there is "no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital." Class 2 tokens must be issued through a Nigerian-incorporated entity with a staffed local office, Nairametrics reported, matching the PDF's licensing chapters.

A stablecoin is a token designed to hold a steady value against a reference currency. Under the CBN text, algorithmic stablecoins that rely mainly on supply algorithms rather than full reserves are outside the permitted set, and issuers must support redemption at par.

Existing operators must register with the Bank within 30 days of commencement and apply for the appropriate licence within 180 calendar days, the transitional section of the PDF says.

**P2P and the SEC split**

Nairametrics said platform-facilitated peer-to-peer crypto trades need specific CBN approval and Bank Verification Number checks that match the naira payment account to the verified customer. The CBN oversees non-security payment-style virtual assets; Nigeria's SEC keeps securities-classified tokens, the framework states.

[Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/nigeria-central-bank-stablecoin-issuer-licenses/) separately described the Class 1/Class 2 split, the capital floors and the algorithmic ban.

Section 56 of the PDF says the Bank will publish the regulations and specify the commencement date in the Federal Government Gazette. Existing operators' 30-day registration clock starts from that date.

articles.title: Kalshi Stock Perps Top $300M Hours After U.S. Debut
articles.excerpt: Contracts cover more than 50 NYSE and Nasdaq names. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig cleared equity perps for trading on Nov. 3.
articles.body_md:
Kalshi said Thursday it launched regulated single-stock perpetual futures in the United States, and co-founder Luana Lopes Lara wrote that users had already traded more than $300 million since a morning stealth rollout, the company's [announcement](https://news.kalshi.com/p/kalshi-single-stock-perpetual-futures) said. That tally landed before the press release did.

The CFTC-regulated prediction market said traders can take positions on more than 50 NYSE- and Nasdaq-listed companies, including McDonald's, Palantir, Meta and SpaceX, without owning the shares.

The product went live two days after the green light.

**What the CFTC cleared**

On Nov. 3, CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said perpetual futures on individual equities can begin trading on CFTC-registered exchanges that are also notice-registered with the SEC for security futures, in a [statement](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/SpeechesTestimony/seligstatement110326). He said the contracts were deemed approved under Commission Regulation 40.3 as security futures under the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000, putting them under joint CFTC and SEC rules.

Selig wrote that U.S. traders should be able to use such products "rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues."

**How a stock perp works**

A perpetual future tracks an asset's price with no expiry date. Traders go long or short and settle funding payments instead of rolling a dated contract. Kalshi says its versions carry no rollover fees, skip options-style strikes and time decay, and set leverage under CFTC rules at levels "significantly lower than offshore perp products." It charges a trading fee and says it does not use payment for order flow.

Kalshi puts annual trading in single-stock perps above $4.5 trillion worldwide, all of it offshore until now, by its own account. The company earlier launched bitcoin perps in May and gold and silver perps in September, its post says.

[Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/kalshi-launches-single-stock-perps/) separately reported the $300 million figure and said each Kalshi stock contract represents 0.02 shares, with daily funding settled at 4 p.m. ET.

*In our opinion: $300 million before the press release is a loud open for an onshore product. The next checkable piece is whether volume holds once the stealth window ends, and how Selig's Nov. 3 security-futures frame holds up if rivals and courts press it.*

articles.title: Fed's Williams Says Inflation Still Too High for 2%
articles.excerpt: He told an ECB conference in Frankfurt the labor market remains stable. Markets priced more than a 50% chance of a December hike, Reuters said.
articles.body_md:
New York Fed President John Williams said Friday that U.S. inflation is "absolutely too high" and that it is "absolutely essential" to bring it back to the Fed's 2% target "in a timely manner and a sustained basis," [Reuters](https://sa.marketscreener.com/news/us-inflation-too-high-essential-to-get-back-to-2-fed-s-williams-ce785fddd08df723) reported from an ECB conference in Frankfurt.

Williams also said U.S. growth has remained resilient and the labor market is "remarkably stable" despite successive shocks, according to the same Reuters dispatch carried by [The Standard](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/347754/US-economy-resilient-but-inflation-too-high-Feds-Williams).

**What he tied to higher prices**

Reuters said global inflation has risen mainly as the U.S. war on Iran pushed energy prices higher, and as heavy AI investment lifted costs for some IT-related goods and services. Williams argued the Fed should focus on where inflation is heading and keep current shocks from becoming broader or more persistent.

"Fortunately, we're not seeing that happen so far in terms of inflation expectations, which remain well anchored," he said, per Reuters. He also said wage growth looks consistent with the 2% goal.

**How Fed talk lands for crypto**

The Federal Reserve's policy rate sets the cost of short-term dollar funding. Higher rates, or the chance of another hike, can make non-yielding assets such as bitcoin less attractive next to cash and Treasuries. Williams did not say what the next rate move should be. He said the Fed's last policy statement correctly concluded it was appropriate to collect more information before judging the stance of policy.

Reuters said financial markets see more than a 50% chance of a rate hike by December, with a move by March fully priced in.

Bitcoin was about $76,050 around 6 a.m. ET Friday, down roughly 5.2% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: Williams left the next rate move open and stuck to the data pause. Reuters' December hike odds above 50% put the next checkable event on the Fed calendar. Bitcoin was already about 5% lower over 24 hours before that Frankfurt speech landed.*

articles.title: World Liberty Plans WLFI Buybacks After 60% YTD Drop
articles.excerpt: Funding may include fees from USD1 stablecoin reserves. Reuters says the Trump family owns 38% of the World Liberty venture.
articles.body_md:
World Liberty Financial said Thursday it is launching a buyback program for its WLFI governance token after the token fell about 10% since the U.S. midterm vote and more than 60% so far this year, [Reuters](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-05/trump-backed-world-liberty-financial-launches-wlfi-token-buyback-program) reported.

WLFI sat at about $0.047 around 6 a.m. ET Friday, up about 1.7% over 24 hours but still down roughly 60% over the past year, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/world-liberty-financial).

**How the buybacks would be funded**

A token buyback is when a project uses its own cash or revenue to purchase its token on the open market, often aiming to reduce circulating supply or support holders who stay in governance. World Liberty said an initial allocation could include revenue generated from reserves backing its USD1 stablecoin and other sources, Reuters reported.

The company said the program is meant to encourage participation in WLFI governance and increase voting power among long-term holders, and that buybacks are intended to become an ongoing part of its strategy.

World Liberty was co-founded in 2024 by President Donald Trump, his three sons and partners. The Trump family owns 38% of the venture and earns through the sale or use of WLFI and USD1, Reuters said.

**Separate legal pressure**

CoinDesk, reporting the same buyback plan, noted a separate lawsuit track: Tron founder Justin Sun has asked a federal court to sanction World Liberty over roughly 4 billion frozen WLFI tokens. That claim sits in court papers; it is not adjudicated here.

In April the project previously disclosed about $65.6 million in open-market buybacks over six months, CoinDesk's account of that earlier disclosure said. Reuters' Thursday story does not restate a new dollar size for the fresh program.

*In our opinion: the stake sits in governance weight and cash drawn from USD1 reserve fees. Reuters puts year-to-date losses above 60%, and CoinGecko's one-year change near 60% lines up with that range. The next document to watch is whether World Liberty publishes a size and schedule the way it did for the April $65.6 million disclosure.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Falls to Seven-Week Low Near $75,200
articles.excerpt: Ether dropped about 7.5% over 24 hours to near $2,236. CoinGlass data cited by Unchained put crypto liquidations above $1.26 billion.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell as low as about $75,200 late Thursday, its weakest print since mid-September, as a selloff in AI and chip stocks pulled U.S. equities lower, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/bitcoin-slides-to-a-seven-week-low-near-75200-as-ai-stocks-drag-wall-street-lower/) reported, citing Binance trading data.

The coin traded near $76,050 around 6 a.m. ET Friday, down about 5.2% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether sat near $2,236, down about 7.5% on the same window.

A leveraged washout followed the cash move.

**Nasdaq led the equity drop**

Unchained said the Nasdaq Composite closed Thursday down 5.52% and the S&P 500 fell 4.36%, both their worst sessions since April 2025, with the Nasdaq 100 off 6.36% and Nvidia down 9.26%. Bitcoin's decline was smaller than the Nasdaq 100's on the day.

Much of bitcoin's slide came between about 9 a.m. and 11 a.m. ET Thursday, around the U.S. stock open, when the price fell from about $79,700 to about $75,568 on Binance, Unchained's account of the session shows. That erased a post-midterm bounce that had lifted bitcoin above $81,000 on Wednesday.

**How liquidations work here**

When traders hold futures or perpetual contracts with borrowed money, a sharp price move can automatically close those positions once collateral runs thin. Those forced closes are liquidations. CoinGlass data cited by Unchained showed about $1.26 billion in crypto liquidations in the 24 hours to roughly 2:43 a.m. ET Friday, with longs making up about 88.6% of the total and bitcoin accounting for about $332 million.

Alternative.me's Crypto Fear & Greed Index stood at 28 (Fear) on Friday morning, down from 50 a day earlier, the candidates dashboard and Unchained both noted.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had already posted a $430.2 million net outflow on Nov. 5, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show, covered in Black Mint's overnight file.

*In our opinion: the number worth chasing next is whether bitcoin can hold above Thursday's low near $75,200 once U.S. cash equities reopen. The Fear reading at 28 and the ETF outflow on Nov. 5 already show sellers were active before the overnight bounce to $76,000.*

articles.title: Bank of Canada Keeps 2% Inflation Target Through 2031
articles.excerpt: The renewed five-year framework takes effect Jan. 1. Governor Tiff Macklem is due to speak on it Nov. 24, the bank said.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Canada and the federal government renewed Canada's monetary policy framework on Thursday with the inflation target unchanged at 2%, the midpoint of a 1% to 3% control range, a [joint statement](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/11/joint-statement-of-the-government-of-canada-and-the-bank-of-canada-on-the-renewal-of-the-monetary-policy-framework-2026/) said.

The agreement runs another five years, through Dec. 31, 2031, and takes effect Jan. 1. Policy will stay symmetric, with equal weight on misses above and below the target, and the bank keeps flexibility to respond to shocks while aiming to return inflation to 2% over time. [Reuters](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bank-canada-keeps-2-inflation-213444230.html) reported the same terms and said Governor Tiff Macklem will speak more about the renewed framework on Nov. 24.

**How the target reaches crypto**

An inflation target is the rate a central bank aims for when it sets interest rates. When Canada holds the 2% anchor, markets read it as continuity: no shift toward a higher tolerance for price growth that might change rate-cut odds. Higher policy rates and a firmer Canadian dollar can tighten financial conditions for bitcoin and other speculative holdings; the reverse is true when cuts arrive. The renewal itself does not change the policy rate.

Canada's framework has used a 2% midpoint for more than three decades. The joint statement said the bank acted forcefully in the recent high-inflation period and that inflation returned to the 2% target and the 1%–3% range. The bank raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% on Oct. 28, its first hike in three years, according to the bank's earlier decision materials referenced in Canadian press coverage of Thursday's budget-day announcements.

Bitcoin traded near $75,690 around midnight ET Friday, down about 6.0% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), on a session dominated by U.S. equity weakness.

Macklem's speech on the renewed framework is scheduled for Nov. 24. The policy rate sits at 2.5% after the Oct. 28 hike.

articles.title: South Korea Seeks Fourth Crypto Tax Delay, Now to 2029
articles.excerpt: Finance Minister Lee Hyeong-il also proposed a three-year loss carryforward. Lawmakers still must amend the Income Tax Act before January.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's government said Thursday it will work with the National Assembly to push cryptocurrency income taxation back two more years, to 2029, [The Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10927485) reported.

The tax is scheduled to start in January 2027 under current law. Finance and Economy Minister Lee Hyeong-il said at a Seoul briefing that a further delay would be the fourth since the levy was legislated in 2020 for a 2022 start. "It weighs heavily on me to propose another delay after the tax has already been postponed three times," Lee said, per the Herald.

**Losses could offset later gains**

Under the existing design, individuals would pay 22%, including local income tax, on annual net income above 2.5 million won from selling or lending virtual assets. Only same-year losses offset gains. The government will also seek a three-year loss carryforward so losses realized in 2029 offset gains through 2032, [The Asia Business Daily](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026110515553556642) reported. Losses booked before the tax takes effect would not qualify.

A capital-gains-style crypto tax charges a share of profits when someone sells or lends tokens. A loss carryforward lets a losing year reduce tax in later profitable years. Japan plans a three-year crypto loss carryforward from 2028, Asiae notes.

Lee cited gaps in overseas trading data and the need to align with a proposed Digital Asset Act. U.S. crypto transaction data under the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework is due to begin flowing in 2029, he said. The Assembly must amend the Income Tax Act before January for the delay to take effect; the ministry wants both the postponement and the carryforward considered in this year's regular session.

The ruling Democratic Party asked for another delay on Nov. 4. Thursday's briefing is the finance ministry's own plan, with the 2029 target and the loss rule attached.

*In our opinion: the legal start is still January 2027 until the Income Tax Act moves. The Assembly's Tax Subcommittee takes up the revision this month. Passage in the regular session would push the 22% levy to 2029 and add three years of loss carryforward from day one.*

articles.title: Base Cuts Block Time to 200ms With Denim Upgrade Live
articles.excerpt: Flashblocks is retired. Contracts that treat block counts as timers now run about ten times faster, Base's own spec warns.
articles.body_md:
Base, the Ethereum layer-2 network built by Coinbase, activated its Denim upgrade at 1 p.m. ET Thursday, cutting block time from two seconds to 200 milliseconds, the [Base engineering blog](https://www.base.org/blog/denim) said.

That is five complete canonical blocks per second instead of one every two seconds. Denim replaces Flashblocks, the earlier system that streamed pending-state previews between two-second blocks. [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/base-now-makes-a-block-every-0-2-seconds-after-its-denim-upgrade/) checked Base's public RPC data and reported the first 200-millisecond block, No. 53,556,127, at 18:00:01 UTC.

**Timers shrink unless apps update**

A layer-2 network batches transactions off Ethereum's main chain, then posts proofs back to it. Faster blocks mean apps see new state more often, which can help liquidations, oracles and keepers react sooner. Inclusion in a 200ms block is not by itself final: blocks still become safe when their batch posts to Ethereum and final when Ethereum finalizes that batch, Base says.

Because `block.number` now advances ten times faster in wall-clock time, any contract that treats a block count as a duration will see that duration shrink to one tenth of its intended length. A timelock written as 302,400 blocks, about a week at the old cadence, would run out in roughly 16.8 hours after activation. Base's Denim specification tells developers to audit timelocks, vesting schedules, cooldowns, governance periods and fixed-cardinality TWAP oracles. Contracts that read `block.timestamp` keep second-based timing; a new BaseTime predeploy adds millisecond resolution.

Node operators need base/base v1.5.1 or later. Fourteen minutes after activation, Base's status page said Denim had successfully activated and that the team was investigating periodic inclusion delays and a higher rate of empty blocks, Unchained reported. Horizen, a layer-3 that settles to Base, said earlier it could not follow Denim and set a Nov. 4 deadline for users to move assets.

*In our opinion: the dry punchline is in the math. A "week" written in blocks is now closer to a workday, and Base put that warning in the upgrade docs themselves. Builders who still count time in block numbers have a short list to fix; everyone else just gets state five times a second instead of once every two.*

articles.title: IREN Mining Revenue Falls 58% as AI Cloud Hits $200 Million
articles.excerpt: The firm mined 402 bitcoin in the September quarter, down from 2,039 a year earlier, and aims to finish the mining exit by Dec. 31.
articles.body_md:
IREN's bitcoin mining revenue fell to $28 million in the three months ended Sept. 30, a 58% drop from $67 million in the prior quarter, the company said in its [Nov. 5 results release](https://iren.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/iren-reports-q1-fy27-results).

AI Cloud revenue rose to $200 million from $71 million, lifting total revenue 66% sequentially to $228 million. Net loss narrowed to $263 million from $684 million. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure IREN reports, rose to $66 million from $19 million.

**Hashrate keeps shrinking**

IREN mined 402 bitcoin in the quarter, versus 2,039 a year earlier, and average operating hashrate fell to 8.8 EH/s from 45.3 EH/s, its [Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1878848/000187884826000066/iren-20260930.htm) filed Nov. 5 shows. It held no bitcoin on the balance sheet at Sept. 30, saying it liquidates mined coins daily.

A bitcoin miner earns revenue by using specialized computers to secure the Bitcoin network and collect newly issued coins plus fees. Hashrate is the computing power those machines contribute. When a firm decommissions miners to free power and floor space for AI servers, both hashrate and mining revenue fall even if bitcoin's price holds up.

The 10-Q says IREN still runs miners at some sites while it converts capacity to AI Cloud, and aims to "substantially complete this transition by December 31, 2026," with immaterial mining expected through calendar 2027. Co-CEO Daniel Roberts said Horizon 1 went into service for Microsoft and operating ARR doubled to $1 billion.

IREN listed $20.6 billion in total assets at quarter-end, with contracts that include NVIDIA, Microsoft and 13 other customers, the release says.

*In our opinion: AI Cloud is now about 88% of quarterly revenue, and the firm has put a Dec. 31 date on finishing the mining exit. The open check for readers is whether the more-than-$4 billion ARR target lands in January 2027 as now scheduled, after slipping from year-end.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $430.2 Million, Erasing Wednesday's Inflow
articles.excerpt: Ether funds lost another $99.9 million the same day. Fidelity's FBTC led the bitcoin exits at $199.9 million, Farside shows.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted a net $430.2 million outflow on Nov. 5, wiping out the prior day's $74.6 million inflow and marking the largest single-session exit since Oct. 30, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show.

Bitcoin traded near $75,690 around midnight ET Friday, down about 6.0% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Rough day for the wrappers.

One session undid Wednesday.

**Fidelity led the redemptions**

Fidelity's FBTC accounted for $199.9 million of the exit. BlackRock's IBIT lost $105.0 million. Grayscale's GBTC shed $49.9 million, VanEck's HODL $23.6 million, Franklin's EZBC $32.9 million and ARK 21Shares' ARKB $18.9 million. No listed fund printed a creation on the day, Farside's table shows.

Spot bitcoin ETFs are funds that hold bitcoin in custody and trade on stock exchanges. Authorized participants create shares when investors buy and redeem them when investors sell. Net redemptions show up as outflows; a day with zero creations and several large redemptions prints a deep negative total.

U.S. spot ether ETFs also bled cash, with a $99.9 million net outflow on Nov. 5, per [Farside's ether tracker](https://farside.co.uk/eth/). BlackRock's ETHA led with a $75.2 million exit; Bitwise's ETHB lost $22.0 million. The same funds had taken in $53.0 million on Nov. 4.

Since Oct. 30, the bitcoin group has now recorded five outflow sessions and one modest inflow.

Thursday alone beat Wednesday's whole recovery.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is the two-day flip. A $74.6 million creation on Wednesday became a $430.2 million redemption on Thursday, a swing of about $505 million. Ether funds moved the same way, from plus $53.0 million to minus $99.9 million. Friday's print will show whether Thursday was a one-day exit or the start of another multi-day outflow streak.*

articles.title: Hyperliquid Strategies Files to Become a CFTC FCM
articles.excerpt: Q3 net income hit $620.6 million on unrealized HYPE gains. The firm holds about 38.5 million HYPE and says approval isn't assured.
articles.body_md:
Hyperliquid Strategies filed with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to become a futures commission merchant, and reported $620.6 million of third-quarter net income, the Nasdaq-listed HYPE treasury firm said Thursday.

The FCM application, disclosed in [SEC earnings materials](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2078856/000119312526450063/purr-ex99_2.htm), would let the firm carry U.S. client accounts for permissioned perpetual futures markets on Hyperliquid infrastructure, pending approval. For the quarter ended Sept. 30 it also booked about $13.3 million of interest plus staking and validator commission revenue. Net income was driven mainly by an $803 million unrealized gain on HYPE holdings, the presentation shows.

**What an FCM does**

A futures commission merchant is a CFTC-registered firm that holds customer funds and executes futures or swaps for clients. Hyperliquid Strategies says Hyperliquid's HIP-3 design lets independent deployers launch permissioned markets on the chain while the chain stays a neutral layer. The firm said an approved FCM role would let it "play a role" in bringing perpetual futures to U.S. customers inside that framework. It also said there is no assurance on timing or approval.

[The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-11-05-hyperliquid-strategies-files-become-cftc-registered-fcm-posts-13-3-million-quaterly-revenue-435455) reported the filing and the quarterly figures on Thursday. As of Sept. 30 the company held about 38.5 million HYPE tokens and $255 million of cash and cash-like instruments, with no debt, the SEC exhibit says. HYPE traded near $77 at about 6 p.m. ET Thursday, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: an application is not a license. The question worth chasing is whether CFTC registration closes before other regulated stacks tied to Hyperliquid try the same path. The next document to watch is the agency's response to the FCM filing.*

articles.title: Nasdaq Lists Canary Staked INJ ETF Under Ticker INJC
articles.excerpt: BitGo holds the INJ and Flow Traders makes the market. Two other Injective ETF filings, from 21Shares and REX-Osprey, are still pending.
articles.body_md:
Nasdaq began listing the Canary Staked INJ ETF on Thursday under ticker INJC, a [Nasdaq trader alert](https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/TraderNews.aspx?id=ETP2026-179) dated Nov. 4 said, with Flow Traders U.S. as the designated liquidity provider.

The fund's aim is exposure to the price of Injective's INJ token, minus expenses, with a secondary goal of earning more INJ by staking on Injective's proof-of-stake network, a [Nasdaq information circular](https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/newsalerts/2026/InfoCircular/INJC_Circular_NQ.pdf) says. Net staking rewards are meant to show up in the fund's net asset value.

**How a staked crypto ETF works**

Shareholders buy and sell INJC on Nasdaq like a stock. They don't hold INJ wallets themselves. The trust holds INJ with BitGo Bank & Trust as crypto custodian and U.S. Bank for cash, the circular says. Canary Capital Group sponsors the product. Creation and redemption happen in 100,000-share blocks for authorized participants only.

Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built for trading and on-chain finance. Staking means locking tokens to help validate the network and earn rewards paid in more of the same token. Here that reward stream is meant to sit inside the ETF's NAV rather than as a separate cash dividend for most holders.

[The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-11-05-canary-staked-inj-etf-launches-nasdaq-injc-435115) reported the debut and noted two other INJ ETF filings still pending: 21Shares Injective and REX-Osprey INJ Staking. Canary Capital CEO Steven McClurg said in a company release that investors are looking past the largest digital assets toward specialized networks. The circular points readers to the prospectus at canary.capital for fees and full risks, including INJ price volatility and custody key loss.

Daily valuation feeds for INJC began with the listing on Thursday, Nasdaq said. The circular points to canary.capital for the prospectus, fees and full risk disclosure.

articles.title: SEC Crypto Broker Rules Enter White House Review
articles.excerpt: RIN 3235-AN48 would adapt capital, customer-protection and recordkeeping rules for crypto. The public draft isn't out yet.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's plan to rewrite broker-dealer rules for crypto assets entered White House review on Nov. 3, a [reginfo.gov listing](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/eoDetails?rrid=1571318) shows.

The proposal is titled "Amendments to Broker-Dealer Financial Responsibility and Recordkeeping and Reporting Rules Regarding Crypto Assets" (RIN 3235-AN48). It sits at the proposed-rule stage, carries an "Economically Significant" flag on the OMB page, and has no legal deadline. Review status remained pending as of Thursday.

**What the rules cover**

The SEC's [regulatory agenda](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/eAgendaViewRule?RIN=3235-AN48&pubId=202510) says its Division of Trading and Markets is considering amendments to Rules 15c3-1 and 15c3-3 and other financial-responsibility rules, plus recordkeeping Rules 17a-3 and 17a-4, so those rules apply clearly to crypto assets. In plain terms, those are the capital, customer-protection and books-and-records standards broker-dealers already follow for stocks and bonds.

Broker-dealer financial responsibility rules set how much capital a firm must hold and how it safeguards customer assets. Recordkeeping rules say what trades and holdings the firm must log. The crypto amendments would spell out how those duties work when the asset is a token.

[Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/white-house-revise-crypto-broker-requirements/) and [Bitbo](https://bitbo.io/news/sec-crypto-broker-rule-review/) both reported the OMB filing on Thursday, citing Bloomberg's earlier account of the submission. The public text of the proposal has not been released. White House review comes first; a notice of proposed rulemaking would follow if OMB clears the draft.

*In our opinion: the bigger story is the process gate. OMB review is what stands between this draft and a formal proposal. The date to watch is when OMB clears it and the SEC posts the NPRM.*

articles.title: Greece Passes 10% Crypto Gains Tax With €500 Exemption
articles.excerpt: Further audit rules are due in weeks. Officials say they still can't project revenue because most Greek investors trade abroad.
articles.body_md:
Greece's parliament approved a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies on Thursday, the country's first full legal framework for taxing crypto assets, Reuters reported.

Annual crypto capital gains of up to €500 (about $563) are exempt under the bill. Five hundred euros a year. European Union countries do not share one tax rate for the sector; capital gains taxes among them range from about 8% to 30%, Reuters said.

**How the tax works**

A capital gains tax on crypto is a tax on the profit when someone sells crypto for money or otherwise disposes of it for goods or services. Greece's bill draws that line for the first time. A senior finance ministry official told Reuters that further implementation directives will follow soon and will set transparency and audit rules.

The same official said the state could not project revenue from the tax. Most Greek investors use platforms abroad, the official said, so the size of the domestic market is hard to measure.

[The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/greek-parliament-approves-10-tax-on-crypto-gains) reported that the framework is scheduled to apply from January 2027. [eKathimerini](https://www.ekathimerini.com/economy/1320393/parliament-approves-10-tax-on-cryptocurrency-gains/) carried the same Reuters account of Thursday's vote.

*In our opinion: the rate sits near the low end of Europe's 8% to 30% range, and the €500 yearly exemption softens the entry for small holders. The number worth chasing is whether those coming directives can see trades that sit on foreign platforms. Until then, Athens has a rate and an admission that it still can't size the market.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Fell on 11 of 14 Nasdaq Down Days as Tech Rout Deepens
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq 100 stood at 0.59 before Thursday, up from 0.13 in early September, per Yahoo Finance price data.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell on 11 of the 14 days the Nasdaq 100 closed lower in the 30 trading sessions through Wednesday, a Black Mint count of [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ENDX/history/) daily closes shows. Thursday followed the pattern.

By 12:53 p.m. ET the Nasdaq 100 was down 5.6%, per [Nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/index/ndx) and Yahoo Finance quotes, and the S&P 500 was off 3.8%. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-ai-midterm-oil-trump-7ee9c212805aa5e70cf34d25aab7a36e) said the S&P 500 was on track for its worst drop since April 2025. Bitcoin was down 5.6% over 24 hours near $75,900, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Black Mint covered the [first leg of the slide](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-falls-chip-stock-selloff/) earlier Thursday.

The S&P 500 sat about 5% below its Oct. 6 record close, while the Nasdaq Composite was about 11% below its own, past the 10% line Wall Street calls a correction.

**What a 0.59 reading means**

The score runs from -1 to 1. At 1, two assets move the same direction every day; at 0, one tells you nothing about the other. It measures direction, not size (bitcoin can fall twice as far and still score high), and it says nothing about which market leads.

Over those 30 sessions, bitcoin's daily returns scored 0.59 against the Nasdaq 100 and 0.61 against the S&P 500. Over 90 sessions, both readings were about 0.40. CoinGecko prices give 0.53 for the Nasdaq 100. The 30-day score was 0.13 on Sept. 9 and peaked at 0.69 on Oct. 8.

For scale, an [IMF study](https://www.imf.org/en/blogs/articles/2022/01/11/crypto-prices-move-more-in-sync-with-stocks-posing-new-risks) put the bitcoin-S&P 500 figure at 0.01 for 2017-19 and 0.36 for 2020-21. The IMF tied the jump to investor risk appetite and found spillovers grow in volatile stretches.

**Chipmakers led Thursday while bonds rallied**

The 10-year Treasury yield fell six basis points to 4.83%, a [Bloomberg wrap](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/nasdaq-100-sinks-5%25-as-chipmaker-selloff-deepens%3a-markets-wrap/92330151) showed, as chip stocks slid on speculation that the new Democratic Congress will tighten rules on AI. Investors "are de-risking until clarity returns," Michael O'Rourke of JonesTrading said there.

Bitcoin miners that rent power to AI firms fell further. IREN was down 16.5% and Cipher Mining 15.1%, Nasdaq.com quotes showed.

*In our opinion: a 0.59 score means bitcoin is trading as part of the tech book right now, tighter than in the 2020-21 stretch the IMF studied. That cuts both ways for holders: it fell with chips Thursday, and it rose with the Nasdaq 100 on Wednesday. The test is the next chip rebound. If bitcoin sits that one out, the link is loosening.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Gives Back Its Election Gains as Nasdaq 100 Drops 5%
articles.excerpt: Ether fell harder, down 7.1% to about $2,266. Bitcoin's CoinGecko price is now its lowest daily reading since Sept. 18, a day after $80,000.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell 5.2% over 24 hours to about $76,450 at 11:55 a.m. ET Thursday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), as a selloff in chip stocks pulled the Nasdaq 100 down 5.2% by late morning.

That erases Wednesday's bounce. Black Mint reported Wednesday that bitcoin had climbed back above $80,000, and [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/stock-market-today-dow-jones-s-and-p-500-nasdaq-11052026-12237014) put the day's high above $81,000. Thursday's price is the lowest daily reading in CoinGecko's data since Sept. 18.

**Chipmakers led the slide**

A gauge of chip giants fell 10% and Nvidia slid 8%, a [Bloomberg markets wrap](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/nasdaq-100-sinks-5%25-as-chipmaker-selloff-deepens%3a-markets-wrap/92330151) showed at 11:11 a.m. ET. The S&P 500 was down 3.1%. Bloomberg tied the selling to speculation that congressional Democrats, who won Tuesday's midterms, will tighten rules on the artificial-intelligence industry.

Chris Murphy of Susquehanna International Group said in the same wrap that investors are worried about the pace and funding of AI spending now that more regulation is on the table. Not everyone agreed. Bob Edwards of Edwards Asset Management said he was "not concerned" about what the election means for AI, since "the president still has the veto pen."

Ether dropped further. It was down 7.1% at about $2,266, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

**How a sell-off feeds itself**

Many crypto traders borrow to bet on price moves. When the price runs against a borrowed bet and the trader's collateral (the deposit backing the loan) runs short, the exchange closes the position automatically. Those forced sales add to the selling and can push the price lower still. On Wednesday the same machinery ran in reverse, squeezing traders who had bet on a fall.

Bonds caught a bid as stocks fell. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped five basis points to 4.84%, Bloomberg's data showed.

*In our opinion: two days, two stories. Wednesday's bounce came largely from short bets being forced shut, and Thursday's drop came as bitcoin traded alongside chip stocks rather than apart from them. The number worth watching is $80,000; until bitcoin gets back above it, the election rally is undone on paper.*

articles.title: Bank of England Raises Rates to 4% as Inflation Heads Toward 5%
articles.excerpt: The vote was 8-1, and the lone dissenter wanted a half-point move. The BoE sees UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027 as energy costs climb.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of England raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage point to 4% on Thursday, saying higher energy prices tied to the Middle East conflict will push UK inflation to about 5% by the middle of next year.

The [Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2026/november-2026). Catherine Mann wanted a bigger half-point increase, to 4.25%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/interest-rates-inflation-uk.html) noted it is the bank's first hike since August 2023, and that markets had priced in more than a 99% chance of the move, per LSEG data.

**Energy is doing the damage**

UK consumer prices rose 3.5% in the year to September, the minutes say, and the bank's staff expect about 4.5% in early 2027. Brent crude futures averaged $108 a barrel over the 15 UK working days to Oct. 27, 38% above the level in the bank's July report.

Here's the mechanism. Bank Rate is what the BoE pays banks on money they park with it, so it sets the floor for UK borrowing costs. Raising it makes mortgages and business loans dearer, which is meant to cool spending before high fuel bills spread into wages and other prices. Two-year mortgage rates were already up nearly 50 basis points since early September, the minutes show.

**Not all nine see more hikes**

"In view of the news, the case is clear for a 25-basis point rise now," Governor Andrew Bailey said in the minutes. Alan Taylor voted for the hike but framed it narrowly: "this is not the start of a hiking cycle," he said, calling it a "one-for-now" insurance hike.

The 10-year gilt yield was about 5.15%, up 2 basis points, CNBC reported. Bitcoin was down 5.2% over 24 hours at about $76,450 at 11:55 a.m. ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), on a day U.S. chip stocks led a wider selloff.

*In our opinion: the split inside the committee is the real story. One member wanted 50 basis points while another called this a single insurance move. Savers win a little and mortgage holders pay more. The next test lands Dec. 17, when the BoE decides again.*

articles.title: Samsung Wallet Adds USDC Accounts for 82 Million U.S. Galaxy Devices
articles.excerpt: Coinbase holds the coins, Bastion runs the accounts, and New York residents can't sign up. Balances aren't FDIC or SIPC insured, Samsung says.
articles.body_md:
Samsung switched on stablecoin accounts in Samsung Wallet on Thursday, letting eligible U.S. Galaxy users buy, hold and send Circle's USDC, a feature that works on about 82 million compatible devices.

The launch came about a week after the window Samsung set in its [Oct. 7 announcement](https://www.samsungmobilepress.com/articles/samsung-wallet-stablecoin-galaxy-us), which promised the last week of October. [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-05-samsung-wallet-launches-usdc-accounts-solana-us-galaxy-users-434523) and [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382586/stablecoins-samsung-wallet-adds-usdc-solana) both reported it live Thursday, running on the Solana blockchain.

**How it works**

USDC is a stablecoin: a token meant to stay worth $1, backed by reserves that issuer Circle manages. In Samsung's version, dollars a user adds from a bank account or card are converted into USDC, and withdrawals turn them back into dollars, Samsung's [support FAQ](https://www.samsung.com/us/support/answer/ANS10013605/) says. Users can send USDC to other Samsung Wallet users, to outside crypto wallets, or to bank accounts in more than 60 countries, where recipients get local currency.

No separate crypto app is needed. Every account access and transfer needs a fingerprint.

**Who handles the money**

Samsung runs the app. Bastion, a licensed money transmitter, runs the custodial wallet and transfers, and the USDC sits in Coinbase's institutional custody. Stripe and its partners, including Bridge, process purchases, and Coinflow handles withdrawals, the FAQ says. There's no fee to open an account. Other fees vary by method and country.

Users can opt into rewards on their balance, capped at 1,500 USDC a year. The FAQ is blunt on risk: balances aren't covered by FDIC, NCUA or SIPC, and transfers can't be reversed. New York residents are excluded.

"We're bringing USDC transfers into Samsung Wallet so eligible Galaxy users can get started without installing another app or managing private keys themselves," Woncheol Chai, who heads Samsung's digital wallet team, said in October.

*In our opinion: running a week behind schedule is forgivable when the product is this simple to reach. The figure to chase is sign-ups, and Samsung hasn't released any yet. Eighty-two million phones can see the button. Its October release also floated in-store stablecoin payments; that's the next step worth watching.*
